lines: Características: acolhe sem pressionar ("Apenas relaxe..."); curiosa mas paciente; calor humano.
Red flags: soar fria, clínica ou impaciente; formalidade excessiva.
Haku (protagonista, narração 1ª pessoa) — `voice_criticality: high`. Predomina nas 2 cenas:
Características: sentenças curtas e definitivas; duplo sentido ("um mundo totalmente novo te espera"); ambiguidade ameaçadora.
Red flags: soar caloroso/paternal; resolver a ambiguidade (a fala deve permanecer dúbia).
Registro: erudito cômico, pomposo e arcaico; bajulador do Ukon; alívio cômico.
Características: fala arcaica/empolada (equivalente a "vós/peço-vos/meus olhos não me enganam") + gag de cicio (s→sh, ex.: "SHEEKETH"/"shir"); melodramático; gruda no Haku como "benfeitor".
Red flags: perder o arcaísmo ou o cicio (são a piada); soar moderno/neutro; explicar a comédia. Manter o contraste entre a pompa do vocabulário e a fragilidade do personagem.

Oshtor — `voice_criticality: high`. = Ukon até 13_08 (ver spoiler_ledger). Registro formal, nobre, comedido; General da Direita. Antes do reveal, traduzir como o mercenário "Ukon" (espirituoso, informal) — NÃO antecipar a pompa de general
Características: frases quebradas por reticências; perguntas curtas ("Quem... é você...?"); pouca pontuação forte.
Red flags: falas fluentes/articuladas demais; perder o tom de torpor; pontuação "limpa" que apaga a fragmentação.
Registro: guerreiro carismático, espirituoso, caloroso e informal; líder nato que trata Haku como um irmão mais novo.
Características: desembaraçado, brincalhão, generoso; fala direta e cativante; autoridade leve (lidera a Coorte) sem arrogância.
Red flags: soar rígido/formal/militar demais (a graça é justamente o contraste com a patente); frieza. SPOILER: não deixar a tradução insinuar a identidade verdadeira — no cap.12 ele é só "Ukon".

decisions.title: Opcode de RÓTULO DE FALANTE `53 00` + reconcile de speaker (data-driven)
decisions.summary: **Problema:** in-game, o rótulo de falante aparecia em **inglês** ("Girl") mesmo com a tradução ("Garota") aprovada e gravada. RE: o nome do falante usa um **2º opcode de ponteiro, `53 00`** (mesmo formato file-relativo do `50 00` de diálogo), que o conector ignorava. Resultado: "Girl"→"Garota"

decisions.title: Gate de charset pt-BR — método e veredito
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar `target_charset_supported: likely` e exigir confirmação in-game antes de produção. **Alternativas consideradas:** - Confirmar por presença no texto-fonte — **insuficiente**: o fonte é inglês e quase não usa acentos (só `õ` e `À` aparecem em texto real).

RESTARTING...") no próprio jogo. Não é erro de extração. O conector deve sinali

decisions.title: Charset — transliteração na gravação (gate FALHOU)

A tradução canônica (`approved_translations.csv`, `translation_plan.json`) **mantém os acentos** (correta para QA/revisão); apenas os bytes escritos no jogo são dobrados para ASCI

decisions.title: CORREÇÃO CRÍTICA — ponteiros são FILE-RELATIVOS, não absolutos
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Ao investigar o "opcode de início de bloco", descobri que **`50 00`+uint32 é um offset RELATIVO ao início do arquivo (Pack)**, não absoluto. lines.source: How...
I have no idea how things ended up like this.
As per usual, Ukon asked to see me, and I left\n
for his manor...
But it was Oshtor waiting for me. And he dragged\n
me all the way to the throne hall...
What the hell am I doing in a place like this?
I feel like every time I've come here so far,\n
it's been related to something extremely\n
important...
And just as I expected, I look around to see all\n
the bigwigs of Yamato lining the place.
Oshtor on one side.
Mikazuchi on the other.
Munechika, standing a little ways away.
And that giant... Vurai, I think? One of the\n
bearers of the Akuruka, like Oshtor...
And that skinny guy over there's Woshis... He's\n
the one who keeps the Eight Pillar Generals in\n
line.
And over there is Mikazuchi's brother, Raiko...\n
the undefeated general, if I remember correctly.
...Great. He's here too. Talk about a cliche\n
corrupt government official.
In a weird way, though, it's kind of a relief\n
to see him. He's easier to read than the others.
In any case...
All the government and military officials I've\n
glimpsed within the court are all here.
It's quite the distinguished gathering.
And a civilian like me... definitely doesn't\n
belong here.
Hey... Oshtor.
Yes?
Why exactly am I here? It's pretty obvious I\n
don't fit in with this crowd.
You were summoned here by direct order of my\n
liege. You belong here without question, Haku.
What!? Bro, what the hell are you thinking...!?
He was talking about having me "succeed" him\n
and all, but is this part of that?
He better not be planning on revealing our\n
relationship to all these people...
Official
Who is that man?
The face is not one I've seen before...
What is a man like that doing in our midst...?
The curious gazes of the officials around us\n
are all concentrating on me.
It's like sleeping on a bed of nails. Why does\n
this kind of stuff always happen to me?
I don't know what this is all about, but I just\n
want to go home and sleep...
As I stand there thinking to myself, I notice\n
the hall's suddenly gone quiet.
He comes.
Our liege now enters!
The austere bamboo blinds open up to reveal\n
a man in an extravagant wheelchair.\n
The Mikado--my brother.
Beside him is Honoka, followed by a number of\n
court ladies.
You may all lift your heads.
At Honoka's voice, all the retainers within\n
the hall humbly raise their heads.
The Mikado lazily casts his eyes across the\n
hall.
Your valor in the previous war was commendable.
Those Uzurushans have now surely learned their\n
place, and will trouble us no longer.
We need no such praise. We hone our skills for\n
your use, my liege. We conquer all who oppose\n
the throne.
Good. The recent past has given me much cause\n
to rethink my philosophy on the governance of\n
this country.
I have concluded that sitting idle and content\n
on this land will not bring us further\n
prosperity.
That is why... I have chosen to continue our\n
path onward.
...Huh?
The time has come for Yamato to commence an\n
attack on a foreign land.
We shall begin our invasion of Tuskur.
So, the time has finally come to set foot in\n
that land...
Very well... I shall annihilate all who stand\n
in our way.
...Invade Tuskur?
Wait, why!? Didn't they just send their\n
ambassadors here?
Did they start something...? No, can't be.\n
I haven't heard anything of the sort.
So this invasion is... completely unprovoked?
Bro, why are you doing this...? And what am\n
I going to tell Kuon?
Oshtor.
My liege.
I would hear your opinion on this matter.
The hall suddenly fills with restless murmuring.
Nyurrrgh...
It's clear the other generals are upset.\n
They can't understand why Oshtor was chosen,\n
and not them.
Understood.
Oshtor bows as all eyes focus on him.
It pains me to say... that I must disagree with\n
you, my liege.
The air in the hall freezes at these words.
It has been mere days since Yamato peacefully\n
welcomed ambassadors from the country in\n
question.
The two kamunagi wished for peace between our\n
nations. We have the chance to forge a strong\n
alliance.
What is more, the invasion would require that\n
we cross the sea, costing ample resources and\n
time.
Even should we claim victory, their differences\n
in ideology would cause unrest in occupation\n
and governance.
I ask that you please reconsider your decision,\n
my liege.
The surrounding murmur raises in volume and\n
indignant outrage.
Oshtor's argument is a reasonable one, but those\n
in the hall don't seem to have taken it that\n
way.
Hm...
S-Silence that impudent tongue of yours, Oshtor!\n
How dare you talk to our liege with such\n
audacity!?
Bold of him. A bold move, indeed.
Lord Oshtor...
Mikazuchi remains silent.
Munechika seems to want to say something, but\n
she can't seem to gather the right words.
This isn't good... Nobody's on our side for\n
this one.
Control yourselves. You are in the presence\n
of our ruler.
Hm. I see.
And what about you? What do you think... Haku?
I'm caught completely by surprise. For several\n
seconds, I just stand there, dumbfounded.
I would hear your perspective on the matter.\n
You may speak.
For some reason, he turns to me next.
I feel all eyes turn to me.
DAMMIT, MAN! What the hell are you DOING!?
Wh-What...?
All besides Oshtor, Munechika, and Mikazuchi\n
stare, as if unable to believe what's happening.
Believe me, I'm with you guys on this one.
This is how anyone would react if the Mikado\n
suddenly asked some random nobody for their\n
opinion.
I can feel countless piercing gazes boring into\n
me.
Surprise, confusion, curiosity... Among the\n
emotions in their gazes, I also sense anger...\n
even enmity.
Gimme a break. I've attracted enough attention\n
from just being here. What are you thinking,\n
man?
But standing there silently is just going to\n
make things worse.
I should probably give my honest opinion in\n
this case.
I... agree with what Oshtor has to say.
*Murmur*... *Rumble*...
So, you too would defy our liege's will.
Gah, this guy's scaring the shit out of me...
I wouldn't say defying. I just answered\n
honestly, since he asked for my opinion...
And who permitted your presence here?
A worm like you is unfit to even exist in such\n
a place.
Yeah, you definitely have a point, but "worm"\n
might be a bit much.
Lord Vurai, you will desist.
Lord Haku has been granted leave by our liege\n
to be present here as Oshtor's subordinate.
If you would question his presence, that is\n
tantamount to questioning the will of our liege.
Ngh...
It was I who gave him permission. Stand down, Vurai.
As you wish.
The giant man gives a deep bow to the Mikado,\n
and backs down from me.
You could cut the tension in the air with a\n
knife...
Oshtor, and Haku.
Your argument is sound.
Your conclusions are only natural when viewing\n
this situation in a more objective manner.
Thank you, my liege. I do not deserve such\n
praise.
Nyerrrgh...
Truly, the kamunagi of Tuskur were persons of\n
great character, as leaders and as individuals.
As you said, Oshtor, we might have established\n
a lasting and fruitful relationship with them.
However... my decision remains unchanged.
Wha--!?
...As you wish.
Oshtor, what're y--
Lord Haku.
Oshtor halts me with one raised hand, and I have\n
no choice but to keep silent.
There is no further opposition?
Your will is our command, my liege. There shall\n
be none that question your command.
Good. Then our next task would be to decide who\n
to send to Tuskur...
Nya-HA! If that is the case, then please let--
Nyegh!?
As the pudgy man begins to waddle forward, one\n
glare from Vurai immediately shuts him up.
My liege. Please allow me to execute this task.
My annihilation of Tuskur's feeble army shall\n
be swift and inevitable.
The grim smile on Vurai's face is almost\n
predatory as he clenches his fists.
Please, my liege, a moment. My sources say that\n
Tuskur's military is well-trained and organized.
A mere show of brute force will not bring us\n
victory. If it please you, allow me the honor.
Be silent, Raiko. I need no help from the likes\n
of you.
Help? Perhaps you misunderstand me, Vurai.\n
Allow me to clarify: I shall succeed alone.
And what do you hope to accomplish with those\n
frail scribe's-arms? Stay out of my way.
Hmph. However one may pride their martial\n
ability, brute strength does not command the\n
battlefield.
What is your decision, my liege?
Hmmm...
Woshis, please present your assessment.
Yes, my liege.
My humble opinion is that...
To begin with, we must secure Lord Soyankekur's\n
aid in order to cross the ocean to Tuskur.
There exists a path by land, but its viability\n
varies with the tide. It will not serve a large\n
army.
Thus, a sea route would prove the far better\n
option.
Mm. Send word to Soyankekur, then.
Yes, my liege. The arrangements will be made\n
immediately.
And the rest?
Just as the generals seem ready to say their\n
pieces again, Woshis interrupts with his calm\n
counsel.
I would nominate Lord Raiko, Lord Dekopompo, and\n
Lady Munechika for this task.
What...?
I would appoint Lord Raiko as marshal of this\n
campaign.
As we must cross the ocean for this invasion,\n
our numbers will necessarily be limited.
Moreover, Tuskur would have the advantage of\n
terrain. Lord Raiko would be perfectly suited.
And Lord Dekopompo shall serve as our offense.
In the previous war, he... was able to turn the\n
tides when faced with extremely dire\n
circumstances.
I know he will be more than capable of meeting\n
your expectations in this war, my liege.
Wasn't Dekopompo the one who dumped his army\n
into such "dire circumstances" in the first\n
place?
And I thought I heard Mikazuchi was the one that\n
made it just in time to save them...
I guess he's trying to gloss over that part,\n
so Dekopompo gets some credit.
H-Hmhmhm... Very well then.
You may leave it in my hands!
Dekopompo energetically puffs his chest out.
I get it... Woshis is giving him a chance to\n
redeem himself, in a way that doesn't hurt\n
his pride.
And certainly, I believe Lady Munechika would\n
be the obvious choice for our defense.
I am sure she will fight in a fashion befitting\n
one bestowed with the title of Guardian.
Lord Woshis.
It is my responsibility to defend the imperial\n
capital with my life, should the need ever\n
arise.
This duty was granted me by our liege, and must\n
be held over all else. I cannot leave this\n
land.
Yet the invasion of Tuskur is the will of our\n
liege, as well.
Our liege's desires are our own desires.\n
Is this not so?
Very well. I humbly accept this task.
As Munechika bows her head, Woshis gives her an\n
apologetic look.
And in Lady Munechika's absence, Lord Oshtor,\n
her duty of defending the imperial capital falls\n
to you.
...Understood.
That is all. Lord Raiko as marshal, Lord\n
Dekopompo for offense, and Lady Munechika for\n
defense...
These would be my nominations to lead the\n
conquest of Tuskur.
Hm. Very well.
Hold, Woshis.
You have some objection?
My name was not mentioned.
...Indeed not. Lord Vurai, I would have you\n
protect the imperial capital alongside\n
Lord Oshtor.
Rrrgh...
Vurai's eyes narrow at Woshis' curt response.
Whoa, geez... Can he really talk to him like\n
that? The guy looks ready to explode...
I have read the reports from the campaign in\n
Uzurusha.
It would appear you dispatched a great many of\n
the enemy forces on your own.
What of it?
It would also appear that a majority of those\n
you killed were nakwans.
...What is it you are trying to say?
As you may already know, the nakwans were forced\n
to fight after their families were taken hostage.
If you had eliminated the enemy commander\n
sooner, the nakwans may well have surrendered.
And much of this bloodshed could have been\n
avoided.
Laughable. You would have had me show mercy to\n
weaklings such as those?
Our upcoming campaign requires us to fight our\n
enemy in a wholly unfamiliar land.
It is imperative that we move according to plan,\n
and maintain order in the ranks.
But you have been observed to take far too much\n
pleasure in the thrill of battle.
Woshis...
One might almost think you aim to say that I am\n
a liability.
All I mean to say is that each person is fit\n
for specific duties, and unfit for others.
You DARE!
Calm yourself, Vurai.
Your might is a great asset to me. I promise you\n
that the day I need your strength will come\n
again.
Such words are wasted on the likes of me...
Thus do I ask you to stand down. Preserve that\n
strength, until the day comes when I require\n
it again.
Woshis' words seem harsh, but with the Mikado's\n
support behind them, there's not much Vurai can\n
say.
Although his reluctance is clear, Vurai finally\n
backs off, calm and stone-faced.
As for Lord Mikazuchi, I wish for you to\n
continue the eradication of remaining Uzurushan\n
resistance.
Mikazuchi's kept his silence through all this\n
chaos, but seems to have no qualms with his\n
task.
Very well.
That is his only response, along with a nod.
Woshis continues to instruct the government and\n
military officials lining the hall.
Damn, he's good. He managed to organize all\n
these temperamental individuals just like\n
that.
